account:
Something unusual may be being arranged without my knowing its purpose, though I have no proof of wrongdoing. People have repeated a vague claim about a bridge or port change at the bakery. A mill worker associated the baker, freight, innkeeper and neighbour with it, and townsfolk said the builder carried a sack of bread at market. Those are reports, not things I personally verified. I did hear the baker say there was no town charge, that exact quantities and agreed payment could not be recalled, and that future orders needed an agreed price. I do not know which transaction that concerned.

My ten-o'clock mill inspection had no apparent host or report. The secretary says the schedule names no organizer. No council letters were supplied at thirteen, and the account ledgers still have not been located. These empty appointments and vague reports make me wonder whether people are keeping me occupied while arranging something, but ordinary disorganization remains possible. The treasury was previously counted at 128 emeralds and left untouched; I have no evidence of missing money.

The innkeeper has an eighteen-hundred appointment with me in the great hall, specifically with my agreement not to arrive early. Its purpose was not stated to the secretary. That condition, together with the bread report, could fit preparations for a gathering or surprise rather than a genuine bridge or port project. This is only a hypothesis. I have instructed the secretary to ask the baker directly about the rumours, obtain a grain-report contact and locate the ledgers, then report at sixteen-thirty. I am now keeping my fifteen-hundred tea appointment at the neighbour's dockside cottage. I greeted the neighbour and asked for dockside news, but have not yet heard an answer.
